conditions.question: Who has to reconstruct this reasoning without the author present?
Can this step be undone, and at what cost?

enablement.action: compare our strengths and weaknesses with the opportunities and threats outside us

guidance.claim: Distinct from Capabilities: this audits the strengths and weaknesses we have now, judged against the work; Capabilities names the abilities a strategy requires, including those still to gain.
Sanitised weaknesses are the most common SWOT failure.
Strengths only count against a stated goal or competitor. Context-free strengths are trivia.

sections.name: Internal strengths weaknesses
sections.question: Which of our own strengths and weaknesses matter to the work?

guidance.claim: Distinct from Macro-Environment Factors, which lists outside conditions lens by lens; this judges which of them, and which competitor moves, help or threaten the work. The same law may appear in both: once as a fact, once as a threat with an owner.
Draw each opportunity and threat from the PESTLE scan or the competitor profiles, and say which one it came from.
A threat with no owner and no trigger gets noticed only once it lands. Carry each threat that needs a response into Risks & Assumptions, where it gets an owner.

sections.name: External opportunities threats
sections.question: Which outside opportunities and threats matter to the work?

guidance.claim: Six lenses: political, economic, social, technological, legal, environmental.
Weight by industry — legal and political dominate banking and healthtech, environmental dominates construction and energy, social and technological dominate consumer.
Review it after an election, a new law or regulation, or a change in the platforms or technology the work depends on.
Where a condition fixes a limit the work must meet, record it in Constraints too.
For a lens that was checked and holds nothing that affects the work, write 'nothing found', so a reader can tell it apart from a lens nobody checked.

sections.name: Macro environment factors
sections.question: Which political, economic, social, technological, legal or environmental conditions affect the work?
